text: The acidified curd is first left to deacidify, then repeatedly wetted and rubbed with water that may carry Brevibacterium linens, so red bacteria and yeasts colonise the rind. This gives the thin orange smear and pungent, slightly ammoniac smell over a sweet, melting paste.

steps.note: In moulds 7.5–19 cm across, drained unpressed.
Rubbed in two or three wet treatments or more, so the rind turns ivory-orange to red-orange.
At least 21 d, or 14 d for small cheeses.
